identity.description: Probabilistic clusterer: fits a weighted mixture of k Gaussians by EM. Its distinguishing emission is the SOFT assignment — per-row membership probabilities (responsibilities) rather than a hard label — and, because it is a genuine density model, it scores unseen points natively and doubles as an anomaly screen. The price is the elliptical assumption: every cluster is a mean + covariance ellipsoid.

emits.note: the distinguishing output: predict_proba responsibilities — a full membership distribution per row, not a hard label; the fitted params-as-output are the mixture components (weights, means, covariances), each directly readable as a segment profile
argmax of responsibilities (predict); lossy relative to soft-assignment — prefer the soft port downstream whenever the consumer accepts it (an argmax adapter covers the rest)
negative per-sample log-likelihood via score_samples — the density-model dividend: points off the training support score low naturally, no wrapper needed

n_components.note: unlike k-means, a likelihood exists — BIC/AIC across k is the principled selector, cross-checked by silhouette on the hard labels

invariances.why: full-covariance EM is affine-equivariant in principle (the covariance absorbs rescaling), but the k-means initialization, the reg_covar floor, and the diag/spherical covariance options are all scale-dependent — unscaled features destabilize the fit in practice
a nonlinear monotone map changes the density's shape — a Gaussian stops being Gaussian under log, so the likelihood surface and the fit both change
the multivariate Gaussian density is undefined on incomplete vectors; sklearn's EM has no missing-data E-step — impute first
a continuous density on one-hot vertices concentrates mass where no data can lie; categorical structure needs encoding, and heavy-categorical inputs mis-suit a Gaussian likelihood altogether
each component IS a Gaussian: clusters are assumed elliptical (mean + covariance); a skewed or heavy-tailed segment gets split across multiple Gaussians to soak up the mis-fit
a full covariance costs p(p+1)/2 parameters PER component — each component needs n >> p rows or its covariance goes singular; diag/spherical trade that floor against the elliptical expressiveness
off the training support the likelihood decays to zero — assignments out there are driven by the nearest component's tail, and the honest reading is the anomaly-score port, not the cluster-id

featureStats.why: rows-per-component divided by dimensionality bounds covariance estimability — below ~5-10 the full-covariance fit will hit singularities and lean on reg_covar
the elliptical assumption is exactly what skew/heavy tails violate — high values predict component-splitting artifacts and argue for the transform placement
flags the initialization/regularization scale-dependence — large spread means the k-means init lands badly and reg_covar floors the wrong axes

modelMetrics.why: GMM's unique privilege in this family: a real likelihood means BIC gives a principled component-count selection unavailable to distance-only clusterers
keeps GMM comparable to its siblings on the family's shared validation axis — cohesion/separation plus stability, never a holdout AUC
EM is multi-modal — a partition that shifts across reseeds/resamples is a local-optimum artifact, not structure
a mixture weight collapsing toward zero is the overfitted-k signature: the model is paying BIC for a component that owns no data
how 'hard' the soft assignment really is — near 1.0 means k-means would do; near 1/k means the components overlap so much the segmentation may be vacuous

edgeCases.condition: singular covariance (component captures < p rows or duplicated points)
edgeCases.behavior: likelihood diverges as a component collapses onto points; fit aborts or degenerates despite reg_covar
an empty/vestigial component survives in the params with no members
one real segment is modeled as 2-3 stacked Gaussians — the component count stops meaning 'number of segments'
component indices are arbitrary — cluster 2 today is cluster 0 tomorrow; any downstream that persists raw ids across refits silently corrupts
degenerates to a single multivariate Gaussian — a density estimator, not a segmentation

driver.wrapperNeeds: none (fit/predict/predict_proba/score_samples native; as a density model it scores NEW points without any assignment wrapper — the family's exception alongside k-means)
driver.threadSafety: EM fit is single-threaded; predict/predict_proba/score_samples are thread-safe

canBeSeeds.via: soft-assignment→features:tabular adapter (responsibilities as k numeric columns)

placementClaims.why: the Gaussian density is undefined on incomplete rows — EM cannot start
Yeo-Johnson/log directly services the distributional assumption: the closer the marginals are to Gaussian, the fewer components get burned modeling skew

full-covariance EM is affine-equivariant in principle, so scaling is not REQUIRED by the math — but it stabilizes the k-means init and makes reg_covar act uniformly, and it becomes effectively mandatory under diag/spherical covariance
the likelihood needs numeric vectors; but a Gaussian on one-hot columns is a shape mismatch — heavy-categorical inputs belong to mixture-of-categoricals territory, not this sheet
